title: LAN Signal Tensor — 192.168.4.x is just a local coordinate in hyperlocality
insight: 192.168.4.x is NOT an address. It IS a tensor — a local coordinate around a hyperlocality. Each IP is a signal, a relay, a beacon, a piece of silicon. The whole LAN is one surface.

layers.L1_silicon: Physical chips: 9950X3D, i9-14900K, 5800X3D, 5800X, M4, Ryzen5, Threadripper, Intel NUCs, Pixel Titan M2, iPhone Secure Enclave, SoloKey ATECC
layers.L2_signal: WiFi (Aperture/Black Mesa), BLE (5 discoverable radios), 10G fiber, ethernet, USB, NFC
layers.L3_relay: GL-MT6000 routes WAN↔LAN. MikroTik bridges House 1. JetStream bridges House 2. sporeGate bridges WiFi↔ETH (192.168.1.x↔192.168.4.x dual-homed!)
layers.L4_beacon: mDNS announces services. DHCP names announce identity. ARP announces presence. BLE announces proximity.
layers.L5_compute: Ollama on 4 gates (east+north+south+iron). 86+ models. RTX 5090+5070+4060+3070+M4 GPU = 5 GPUs across 2 houses.

legacy_overlays.wireguard_on_ironGate: wg0 10.13.37.7/24, peer=157.230.3.183 (golgi, DOWN), still sending keepalives (32MB sent, 0 received)

sporeGate_dual_home_discovery.note: sporeGate has TWO default routes! eno1→.1 (main LAN) AND wlp3s0→192.168.1.254 (ISP modem directly!)
sporeGate_dual_home_discovery.implication: sporeGate can reach the ISP modem's management interface at 192.168.1.254. It bridges two subnets.
sporeGate_dual_home_discovery.ipv6: sporeGate has public IPv6 on WiFi: 2600:1700:b0b0:5b90:*
